key_insight: V-PaSS improves extrapolative perovskite solar-cell prediction by encoding absorber alloys and device stacks with physics-aware, semantically rich representations instead of treating them as fixed categories.
engineering_relevance: This makes it more practical to screen new perovskite compositions and unfamiliar layer architectures before fabrication, especially for out-of-distribution device designs.
method: Interpolates mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers from 23 pure ABX3 endpoint crystal graphs using Vegard’s law plus learned bandgap bowing.
Encodes device stack order, polarity, and interfacial band offsets with a scientific language model for chemically meaningful layer descriptions.
Combines these representations in a model designed for extrapolation to unseen laboratories, alloys, and transport layers.
evidence_signal: Under an institution-grouped split with unseen laboratories in testing, V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE, beating a gradient-boosted baseline (3.017%) and the best tuned benchmark (2.912%), with larger gains on unseen alloys and new-layer cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on the availability and quality of endpoint crystal graphs, interfacial band-offset information, and assumptions like Vegard interpolation, which may be less reliable for strongly non-ideal materials.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
